In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Israeli military assistance to Mobutu was a major factor in the survival of pro-Western rule in the Congo from the mid‐1960s until 1978.
Israel played a significant role in the Congo's political, economic and military development during this period.
Israel's relations with the Congo were of considerable importance for the development of Israel's foreign relations in Africa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Israeli military involvement in the Congo has been a success, and that the Israeli civilian assistance to that country has been a failure.
the Israeli military assistance to the Congolese government was crucial to its survival and the Israeli economic assistance was not as successful as the Israelis would have hoped.
Israel's involvement in the civil and military dimensions of the Congo crisis was significant and successful.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Congo's importance in Israeli foreign policy in the 1960's was much greater than previously assumed, and that Israeli military assistance was crucial to the survival of the pro‐Western regime in Leopoldsille/Kinshasa from 1960 until the early 1990's, when Mobutu was finally overthrown.
Israel was not merely a minor player in the Congo but rather an important one, and that its involvement there was not a marginal aspect of its African policy but rather a major one.
the Israeli military assistance was a crucial factor in the maintenance of the regime in power, and in the preservation of the country's independence.
